title: [wontfix] Add config asset support
body:
Closes #30114 

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

Yes. Podman can now create and manage configuration assets, then mount them read-only in containers with `podman run --config`. The implementation also exposes config management through the Libpod and Docker-compatible APIs.

```release-note
Add support for creating and managing config assets and mounting them read-only in containers.
```

comments.body: [NON-BLOCKING] Packit jobs failed. @podman-container-tools/packit-jobs please check. Everyone else, feel free to ignore.
Config payload reads and API request bodies are now size-limited. This rejects oversized input before it can trigger unbounded memory allocation.
I assume this is for compatibility with the `docker config` command suite?

Using the secrets manager for this feels incorrect (or perhaps redundant?). How are configs different from secrets as written (aside from having no possibility of different driver implementations, that secrets do support)

Configs currently use the same storage manager in a separate directory, and expose the same drivers as secrets. The distinction is in their API and container mount semantics, not in the storage layer.

I reused it because it already provides the required blob storage and driver support, while a separate storage root keeps config objects isolated.
`docker config` is technically part of swarm, so we've not previously made any effort to support it. @Luap99 @baude @Honny1 Opinions?

> docker config is technically part of swarm, so we've not previously made any effort to support it.

`docker secret` [is also a swarm-only feature](https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/secret/). How's that different from `docker config`? With one exception (please see my 1st point below) `podman config` would be essentially a clone of the currently supported `podman secret` feature.

> If you are on a single node just deploy the file alongside and mount it as regular bind mount.

Maybe I'm coming from a very specific environment (large bare-metal non-k8s clusters), but I feel this would fulfill 2 valuable use cases: 

* **Template rendering/interpolation**: `config` assets are not simply blobs statically mounted inside containers. They [support Go template interpolation](https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/configs/#example-use-a-templated-config), which allows to easily convert immutable config assets (templates) in per-container/service instance configuration.
  * Config-file driven services (Prometheus, Alertmanager, nginx, HAProxy, ...) have always been a hassle to work with compared to env-var driven services (postgres, redis, vault, ...). Supporting `docker/podman config`, this difference almost disappears.
* **Multi-node config**: this would be specific to podman, but with a [shell driver](https://docs.podman.io/en/latest/markdown/podman-secret-create.1.html#secret-drivers) analogous to `podman secret`'s, `config` assets don't have to be limited to single-node deployments. It'd be fairly easy to define a single `config` template for a set of nodes, and store/fetch those from, for example, some `etcdctl put|get`.

Just to add more context on the original issue https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/30114, the goal here is to deploy containerized services in multi-node RHEL Image Mode (or bootc variants) custers via podman `compose.yml` -> `podlet` -> `quadlet` -> systemd (I know that [`docker compose` `config` doesn't support template interpolation](https://github.com/docker/compose/issues/13598), so this should be coupled with a podman compose extension `x-podman.template-interpolation`).

Thank you!

> podman config would be essentially a clone of the currently supported podman secret feature.

Which makes it rather pointless in my eyes compared to the amount of duplication it introduces.
And to be clear the way secrets currently work is also not great IMO, I do not want to commit to more of this. The pattern of pull data from course X to run podman secret create to then podman run --secret... seems so much more complicated, now you have to manage lifetimes of secrets in a separate owned podman store. Ideally the flow is your own secret store -> podman run directly.
Then you cannot forget to remove the secret either.

> Template rendering/interpolation: config assets are not simply blobs statically mounted inside containers. They [support Go template interpolation](https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/configs/#example-use-a-templated-config), which allows to easily convert immutable config assets (templates) in per-container/service instance configuration.

And that is the worst part of it. Templates for what values? For a template to make sense podman needs to provide additional "variables" to the template engine. Who defines what those are? Each user will want more and more. And then you get arbitrarily limited to go templates, the next person wants another template driver, etc...
The best solution is run the template engine of your choice before handing the file to podman with whatever variabled you need to pass to it.

Also podman-compose is a community driven project and not supported by any of the podman maintainers.
If your workflow is compose -> podlet -> quadlet that feels wrong, like you should at most do the transition once and then really just edit the quadlet files and ship them.
You could have the quadlet files stored as templates together with your config files, then run your template engine of choice over them and distribute to the hosts. There are plenty of automation tools capable of this.
